doc.title: Jake Hanna interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Gene Krupa and Red Rodney's pay envelopes
summary: Krupa's kindness: he secretly saved part of Red Rodney's pay before Rodney left for Woody's band.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong

blocks.x: They were with Herman too, right? Were they on the band with you?

Conte was about 16 when he was with Woody back in the 40s, with Dave Tough was the drummer. No he remembered him well. And then he went back with a bop band. I’ll tell you a little story about Gene Krupa. The kind of a guy he was. Nothing was taken for granted. You know Buddy Rich worked so hard to be the king of the drums after Gene. But Gene Krupa was the king of the drums. He was the most famous drummer of all time. He put everybody where they are now. Nicest guy that ever lived. Buddy DeFranco said that too. He said he never worked with a better guy in his whole life this guy. And Red Rodney told me a story. He was with Gene for quite a few years you know. And he was the first guy he let play bop. He played whatever he wanted to play. He used to feature him in “The Man I Love” and he played bop. And then he says, “Hey Gene, I got © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-

a chance to join Woody, you know, he’s got a brand new band.” And Shelly and all the guys, Don Lamond, whose ever there. I forget who was there. And he says, “Oh yeah, that’s okay, Woody’s got a helluva nice new band” he says, “okay Red it’s a been a pleasure having you, I know you did a lot for me.” He says, “You ever save any money? I know I’m giving you two hundred a week.” You know and everybody else was making about a hundred and forty dollars. But he loved Red. “I’m only giving you two hundred. You ever save any money?” “Well no. I spend most of it but I got a couple of bucks so I can go get to join this.” “Well I knew you’d blow it.” He says, “Come on back in the back room.” He brings out the filing things you know, full of these little pay envelopes. And he says, “I put away fifty bucks a week for you. I was paying you two-fifty but I only gave you two hundred.” So he wound up with a couple of thousand dollars so he could go out and join Woody. That’s the kind of a guy Gene Krupa was.
